payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. VK2735 remains…

payload.title: GLP-1s Are Melting Fat — But What About Your MUSCLE?
payload.summary: GLP-1 drugs like Wegovy and Zepbound can produce dramatic weight loss. But when someone loses 40 or 50 pounds, there's an important question most people aren't asking: How much of that weight was fat — and how much was lean mass? Research shows that people taking GLP-1 medications can lose measurable amounts of lean body mass along with fat. So yes, lean mass can decrease. But substantially more fat was lost, meaning overall body composition improved. Now researchers want to know whether they can do even better. payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. payload.summary: Sleep Anxiety, Insomnia, Circadian Rhythms, Chronotypes, Sleep Trackers & How to Sleep Better with Dr. Michael Breus Host Dave Asprey sits down with Dr. Michael Breus, clinical psychologist, sleep specialist, and internationally recognized sleep expert known as The Sleep Doctor, to explore insomnia, sleep anxiety, circadian rhythms, chronotypes, nighttime awakenings, temperature regulation, sleep medications, wearable sleep trackers, and the science of improving sleep quality. The conversation challenges conventional thinking about sleep, including whether everyone needs eight hours, why trying harder to fall asleep can make insomnia worse, and how the body's internal clock influences energy, productivity, and recovery. Dr. Breus explains why he believes fear and anxiety contribute to a substantial proportion of sleep problems. He describes how worrying about falling asleep, waking up at 3 a.m., or feeling exhausted the next day can create a cycle of stress that makes restful sleep increasingly difficult. Dave and Michael explore how cognitive behavioral therapy, emotional regulation, and changing your relationship with sleep may help break that cycle without relying exclusively on medication. The conversation explores why sleeping pills may fail to address the underlying causes of chronic insomnia, how nighttime awakenings can trigger negative thinking, and why the fear of being tired may sometimes become more disruptive than the tiredness itself. Dave shares his experience…

payload.summary: The Miracle Morning, Visualization, Affirmations, Meditation, Morning Routines, Productivity & the Psychology of Success with Hal Elrod Host Dave Asprey sits down with Hal Elrod, bestselling author of The Miracle Morning and personal development expert, to explore morning routines, visualization, affirmations, meditation, productivity, circadian rhythms, habit formation, and the psychology of success. Hal Elrod is the creator of The Miracle Morning, a bestselling book and personal development method that has helped millions improve their daily habits. After surviving a devastating car accident at age 20 and later battling life-threatening cancer, Hal developed a philosophy centered on resilience, personal responsibility, and consistent daily practices. Dave and Hal challenge the idea that success requires waking up at 5 AM. They discuss chronotypes, circadian biology, and why morning routines should work with your natural sleep patterns. Hal introduces his six-part SAVERS framework, explaining how meditation, affirmations, visualization, exercise, reading, and journaling can transform your morning in as little as six minutes. They explore how smartphones disrupt attention, why visualization works best when paired with mental rehearsal, and how these techniques can help overcome procrastination. Hal shares how he used visualization to train for a 52-mile ultramarathon, while Dave discusses advanced meditation, neurofeedback, and the role of emotional states in mental…

payload.title: The Treatment That Made Me 15 Years Younger
payload.summary: Explore House of Evolution: https://daveasprey.com/house-of-evolution/ The Science of Reversing Biological Age with Dr. Tim Cook Host Dave Asprey sits down with Dr. Tim Cook, a physician and longevity medicine expert who previously served as personal physician to two Governors General of Canada, to explore experimental gene therapy, biological age reversal, stem cell re-education, immune rejuvenation, muscle growth, and the emerging science of extending human lifespan. Recorded in the Amazon rainforest in Ecuador, the conversation explores three advanced longevity treatments Dave and Tim are working with through House of Evolution, their venture focused on expanding access to experimental therapies. They discuss how these technologies work, the early results they're observing, and why some treatments are currently available outside the United States. The discussion turns to follistatin gene therapy, an experimental treatment designed to increase a protein involved in muscle growth and maintenance. Dave and Tim share preliminary results, including a reported average nine-year reduction in biological-age measurements, increased lean muscle mass, and reductions in body fat. They examine why preserving muscle and reducing visceral fat may be critical for longevity, particularly as anabolic resistance and sarcopenia become more common with age. This episode is essential listening for anyone interested in biological age reversal, gene therapy, follistatin, klotho, stem cell…

payload.title: I FAGIOLI fanno male? Lectine, acido fitico e quali scegliere
payload.summary: 🫘 I FAGIOLI FANNO MALE? I culturisti li snobbano, vegani e vegetariani li adorano. La verità sta nel mezzo: il fagiolo non è una fonte proteica, ma è un ottimo carboidrato. Va scelto bene e cucinato bene. 🔢 I NUMERI 🔸 Proteine: appena 7–9 g ogni 100 g. Per avere 35 g di proteine servono 450 g di fagioli, con circa 110 g di carboidrati 🔸 Fibre: 200–250 g di fagioli danno circa 30 g di fibra. La glicemia resta stabile perché la fibra rallenta l'assorbimento degli zuccheri 🔸 100 g di fagioli secchi diventano circa 250 g di fagioli cotti 🧪 I CARBOIDRATI "DIFFICILI" Verbascosio, stachiosio e raffinosio sono tri- e tetrasaccaridi che l'amilasi non riesce a degradare: sono loro i responsabili delle famose scoregge. Con ammollo e cottura si riducono in modo importante. ⚠️ LECTINE E FITOEMOAGGLUTININE In vitro agglutinano i globuli rossi. Nel corpo vengono digerite, ma se i fagioli sono cucinati male possono aumentare la permeabilità intestinale e dare stanchezza. 🥫 FAGIOLI IN SCATOLA Il problema non sono gli antinutrienti, è il bisfenolo A delle lattine. Meglio i fagioli secchi o, al limite, quelli in vetro. ✅ COME CUCINARLI 🔹 Ammollo per tutta la notte (per i rossi fino a 12 ore), buttando l'acqua dell'ammollo 🔹 Pentola a pressione per 15–20 minuti 🔹 Usali al posto di pasta e riso, abbinati ad altre fonti proteiche e a un filo di olio extravergine d'oliva 🏆 LA CLASSIFICA 1️⃣ Anasazi: lectine meno aggressive (studio del 1998) 2️⃣ Pinto 3️⃣ Cannellini: una via di mezzo 4️⃣ Rossi: i…

Finally, they examine failure, rejection, resilience, and the psychology of achievement. Roman…
